clue.text: Block Pat's construction with asphalt

indicators.note: a construction is something built up out of parts, so the letters are put together in a new arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A builder named Pat lays a paved block using asphalt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pat's' reads as possessive, but it is 'Pat is': BLOCK and PAT together are rearranged into BLACKTOP.
explanation.definitionFit: Blacktop is the American word for bituminous paving material, the same stuff as asphalt.

clue.text: See 26
One of 10 North Dakota males is on time

indicators.note: in a down light, one part sitting on another is placed directly above it

blocks.note: the US postal code for North Dakota
men are males
t is the standard abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A North Dakota man is punctual, said to be among the ten best.
explanation.walkthrough: Per 5-down, a punctuation mark has been deleted from this wordplay: put COMMA back in front of what the clue gives. The '10' is not 10-across but the Ten Commandments.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ten Commandments are the laws Moses brought down from Sinai, so this is one item of that decalogue.

clue.text: Wrongful act: beginning to enjoy cake

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter, which alone is kept

blocks.note: a tort is a civil wrong in law
the opening letter of enjoy

explanation.surface: A legal complaint: the offence was starting to enjoy someone's cake.
explanation.walkthrough: A tort is a wrong dealt with in civil courts, like negligence or trespass.
explanation.definitionFit: A torte is a rich layered cake of the Central European kind, such as Sachertorte.

clue.text: Autumn tonic drunk in recreational area — it was omitted in the wordplay of four Down clues

definitions.text: it was omitted in the wordplay of four Down clues

indicators.note: a drunk person is unsteady and muddled, so these letters are jumbled
the jumbled letters are placed inside the following word

blocks.note: a park is a public space for recreation
taken as written

explanation.surface: A fall drink is consumed in a park, before the clue turns to explain the puzzle's theme.
explanation.walkthrough: The jumbled letters go inside PARK after its P. The theme words are COMMA, COLON, PERIOD and DASH, each missing from the wordplay of a Down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The thing missing from four Down clues is each time a punctuation sign, so the definition describes the category.

clue.text: Some fakirs cherish alcoholic drink

indicators.note: only some of the letters of the following words are wanted, a run lying inside them

blocks.note: the run of letters across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: Certain Hindu holy men are fond of a strong drink.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits across the join of fakIRS CHerish.
explanation.definitionFit: Kirsch is a clear brandy distilled from cherries, so it is a spirit, an alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Ken's heading for Kwanzaa present on the shelf

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its first letter, which alone is kept
in a down light, one part placed on another sits directly above it

blocks.note: the opening letter of Kwanzaa
now is the present moment
a ledge is a shelf

explanation.surface: Ken the doll is a holiday gift that sits unbought on a store shelf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ken' looks like a name, but it is the word meaning range of understanding, as in 'beyond my ken'. Kwanzaa is an African American cultural holiday in late December.
explanation.definitionFit: Ken is a mainly Scottish word for knowledge or range of understanding, as in 'beyond one's ken'.

clue.text: See 24
One dominating some celebrities could be one who wants power over another people

definitions.text: one who wants power over another people

indicators.note: in a down light, something dominating another stands above it

blocks.note: the Roman numeral for one
the A-list is the set of top celebrities

explanation.surface: Someone who lords it over a few famous people could be a would-be ruler of nations.
explanation.walkthrough: Per 5-down, a punctuation mark has been deleted from this wordplay: put COLON back in front of what the clue gives.
explanation.definitionFit: A colonialist favours ruling other countries and their populations as colonies.

clue.text: An embankment for a legendary gardener?

blocks.note: the article, shortened to its one-letter form
a dam is a bank built to hold back water

explanation.surface: Someone suggests a raised bank of earth as a project fit for a famous gardener.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the definition is playful: the first man was put in Eden 'to dress it and to keep it', making him the original gardener.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis Adam tends the Garden of Eden, so he is the gardener of biblical legend.

clue.text: Stochastic model's basic principle, trendy in retrospect, occupies hierarchical position

indicators.note: looking back in time, so the two words before are read from the end towards the start
whatever occupies a place sits inside it, so these letters go within the position word

blocks.note: a rank is one's position in a hierarchy
a law is a fundamental principle
mod means fashionable, as in the 1960s Mods

explanation.surface: A sentence about a statistical model's founding idea, recently fashionable, taking a high place in some ranking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In retrospect' covers both the principle and the trendy word, read together backwards, and 'model' sits in the definition though it looks like part of the surface's subject.
explanation.definitionFit: A random walk is a stochastic process, a path made of successive random steps, used as a model in physics and finance.

clue.text: Ostensible progenitors — one looking back, the other looking forward

indicators.note: something looking back faces the other way, so this word is read from right to left

blocks.note: one of the progenitors: pa, father
the other progenitor is simply a parent, read the normal way round

explanation.surface: A riddle about two supposed ancestors, one facing the past and one the future, like the two faces of Janus.
explanation.walkthrough: Both pieces come from the single word 'progenitors': a father and a parent, the first facing backwards and the second the normal way.
explanation.definitionFit: Apparent means seeming so but perhaps not really so, exactly the sense of ostensible.

clue.text: Talon breaks around a tooth

indicators.note: something that breaks falls apart, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A bird's claw snaps somewhere near a tooth.
explanation.walkthrough: Per 5-down, a punctuation mark has been deleted from this wordplay: put PERIOD, the American full stop, back in front of the rearranged claw word.
explanation.definitionFit: Periodontal is the dental term for the tissues surrounding and supporting the teeth, such as the gums.

clue.text: Language of Sephardic Jews and some Southeast Asians involving noise

indicators.note: to involve is to take in or include, so one word is placed within the other

blocks.note: the Lao are a people of Laos
a din is a loud noise

explanation.surface: A puzzle in comparative linguistics, linking Jewish and Southeast Asian speech with some racket.
explanation.walkthrough: The Lao are the main people of Laos; their name doubles as the name of their language.
explanation.definitionFit: Ladino, or Judaeo-Spanish, is the Romance tongue historically spoken by the Sephardim expelled from Spain.

clue.text: Sheep do badly with major disappointments

indicators.note: doing something badly means doing it wrong, so the letters come out disordered

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Sheep perform poorly, to their owners' great disappointment.
explanation.walkthrough: Per 5-down, a punctuation mark has been deleted from this wordplay: put DASH back in front of the rearranged sheep words.
explanation.definitionFit: Dashed hopes are expectations that have been crushed, the cause of serious disappointment.

clue.text: One way of paying to prepare wool after direct variation

indicators.note: a variation is an altered version, so the letters of the word before are rearranged
this piece is placed following the other one in the answer

blocks.note: taken as written
to card wool is to comb its fibres before spinning

explanation.surface: A maths term, direct variation, joins a story about paying for wool processing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Direct variation' is a real algebra phrase (y proportional to x), which hides the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A credit card is a plastic card used to buy things on borrowed money, a common method of payment.

clue.text: What you might find in a lab: shirts covering upturned rumps

definitions.text: What you might find in a lab

indicators.note: in a down light, turning a word up reads it from the bottom, back to front
a covering goes round the outside, so these letters wrap the others

blocks.note: tees are T-shirts
butts is American slang for backsides

explanation.surface: A lab scene: lab coats or shirts draped over people's raised backsides.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down light 'upturned' means read from the bottom up; the shirts word splits in two to wrap around the other piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Test tubes are the thin glass cylinders standard in any chemistry laboratory.

clue.text: Chair of committees, ultimately, to consume…

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter of the word is kept

blocks.note: the final letter of committees
to eat is to consume

explanation.surface: The person chairing committees ends up eating, with the ellipsis running on to the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chair of committees' looks like one phrase, but only 'Chair' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A seat is anything to sit on, so a chair is one kind of seat.

clue.text: …only fish

blocks.note: first meaning: single, the one and only
second meaning: a flatfish prized for eating

explanation.walkthrough: Read with the previous clue, the committee chair eats nothing but fish; alone, the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means single or exclusive, as in sole heir, and is also the name of a flat seafood species.

clue.text: Pig call, ample in sound, is unlike anything else

indicators.note: these words are to be heard rather than read, so it is the spoken version that counts

blocks.note: sooey is the call farmers use to summon pigs, and generous means ample

explanation.surface: A hog-calling shout with plenty of volume is said to be unique.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, the Latin phrase rhymes roughly with a hog call followed by a word for plentiful.
explanation.definitionFit: Sui generis is Latin for 'of its own kind', meaning unique and in a class by itself.

clue.text: Went crazy in Othello's title part…

indicators.note: only a portion of the words before is wanted, a continuous run inside them

blocks.note: the run starting near the end of the name and running into the next word

explanation.surface: Someone lost their mind while playing the lead in Shakespeare's tragedy, with the ellipsis leading on.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer lies across othelLO'S TITle; the apostrophe is ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: To lose it is an idiom for losing one's composure or sanity, so lost it is went crazy.

clue.text: …like, for example, Othello garbling "…thine own…"

indicators.note: garbled speech has its parts jumbled, so the quoted letters are mixed up

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: The actor playing Othello fluffs the line 'to thine own self be true', which is really Polonius's.
explanation.walkthrough: Othello does double duty: he is the example in the definition and the one garbling the quoted words.
explanation.definitionFit: Othello is a Moor, a Black character among white Venetians, so he is an example of a person who is not white.

clue.text: Gentle push from group leader in 26 & 2

indicators.note: the leader of a word is the letter at its front, which alone is kept
the single letter is placed inside the word that follows

blocks.note: the answer to 26 & 2 means naked, so a synonym is used
the first letter of group

explanation.surface: A soft shove from whoever heads up a group of 26 & 2.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference gives a word for naked, and NUDE is its synonym here.
explanation.definitionFit: A nudge is a light push, usually with the elbow, to draw attention or prompt someone.

clue.text: Floor put up in movie sketches

blocks.note: the American spelling of storey, a level of a building
to board someone is to put them up as a lodger

explanation.surface: A building level is raised in a scene from a film's preparatory drawings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put up' looks like an instruction to turn the floor round in a down light, but this is an across entry and it means to lodge.
explanation.definitionFit: A storyboard is a sequence of drawings sketching each shot of a film before it is made.

clue.text: Make a new picture with scarlet and green

blocks.note: scarlet is a shade of red
green means inexperienced, as does raw

explanation.surface: An artist paints a fresh picture in scarlet and green.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Green' looks like a colour to go with scarlet, but it means untrained.
explanation.definitionFit: To redraw is to draw again, producing a fresh version of an image.

clue.text: French for "rain"

blocks.note: first meaning: the French preposition meaning 'for'
second meaning: to rain heavily

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a request for the French word for rain (pluie); instead the French word for 'for' is itself an English verb for raining hard.
explanation.definitionFit: The English verb means to rain heavily, while the same spelling is the French preposition corresponding to 'for'.

clue.text: Naked young Tarheel?

blocks.note: UNC, the University of North Carolina, has sports teams called the Tar Heels
a lad is a young man

explanation.surface: A child from North Carolina, the Tar Heel State, runs about without clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: Tar Heel is the nickname of a North Carolinian; the question mark flags that it stands for the state university, UNC.
explanation.definitionFit: Unclad means not wearing clothes, the same as naked.

clue.text: Knight is happy? Yes, but heartless

indicators.note: without a heart, so the middle letter of the word is removed

blocks.note: glad means happy
taken as written

explanation.surface: Asked whether a knight is happy, the reply is yes, but he has no heart.
explanation.walkthrough: Knight is not a title here but a surname: Gladys Knight is the American soul singer of Gladys Knight & the Pips.
explanation.definitionFit: Gladys is the first name of the singer Gladys Knight, so the surname clues the given name.

clue.text: Rap about revolving place for bishop's hosiery

indicators.note: something revolving turns round, so this word is read backwards
about means around, so the first word is wrapped around the other

blocks.note: a rap is a knock
a see is a bishop's diocese or seat

explanation.surface: A rap song about a revolving shop that sells socks for clergy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bishop's' looks possessive; read it as 'bishop is', with 'place for bishop' giving the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A knee sock reaches up to the knee, an item of hosiery, the trade term for socks and stockings.
